short: First Hanoverian monarch of Great Britain, whose reign saw the transition to cabinet government.
full:
George I ascended the British throne in 1714 under the Act of Settlement, which excluded dozens of closer Catholic relatives in favour of the Protestant House of Hanover. He spoke little English and relied heavily on his ministers, inadvertently accelerating the shift of executive power away from the crown towards Parliament.

His reign was challenged almost immediately by the Jacobite rising of 1715, which attempted to restore the Stuart line but was decisively crushed. During his rule, Robert Walpole rose to prominence as the first de facto Prime Minister, establishing a model of cabinet government and parliamentary management that would define British politics for centuries.
